pinyin: chóu rén xiāng jiàn, fèn wài yǎn hóng
literal: enemies · meet, extra · eyes · red
natural: when enemies meet, their eyes burn red

meaning.en: When bitter enemies meet, they are filled with rage.
meaning.zh: 仇人见面，格外愤怒。

examples.zh: 仇人相见，分外眼红，两人一碰面就吵起来。
examples.en: When enemies meet their eyes burn red; the two began to quarrel the moment they met.

examples.zh: 比赛里两个老对手仇人相见，分外眼红。
examples.en: The two old rivals were seething when they met in the match.

usage.en: Often used for personal rivals, sometimes jokingly for sport.
usage.zh: 常用于结仇的人，有时也半开玩笑用于体育对手。

text: 你走你的阳关道，我过我的独木桥
pinyin: nǐ zǒu nǐ de yáng guān dào, wǒ guò wǒ de dú mù qiáo
literal: you · walk · your · Yangguan · road, I · cross · my · single-log · bridge
natural: you take your broad road, I'll take my log bridge

meaning.en: Let each go his own way, with no further dealings.
meaning.zh: 你走你的大路，我走我的小路，各走各的，互不相干。

examples.zh: 既然意见不合，你走你的阳关道，我过我的独木桥。
examples.en: Since we disagree, you take your road and I'll take mine.

examples.zh: 他们分手时说：你走你的阳关道，我过我的独木桥。
examples.en: At the break-up they said: you take your road and I'll take mine.

usage.en: Said when parting ways; the tone can be bitter or calm.
usage.zh: 分道扬镳时说，语气可冷淡，也可平静。

pinyin: lái zhě bù shàn, shàn zhě bù lái
literal: come · person · not · good, good · person · not · come
natural: one who comes is not friendly, a friendly one wouldn't come

meaning.en: Visitors who arrive looking for trouble mean no good.
meaning.zh: 上门的人不怀好意，怀好意的人不会来。

equivalents: he who comes in anger has bad intentions

examples.zh: 来者不善，善者不来，大家小心点。
examples.en: He who comes means no good; be careful, everyone.

examples.zh: 这帮人来者不善，善者不来，肯定是来找茬的。
examples.en: This lot mean trouble; they're here to pick a fight.

usage.en: Often a warning when unexpected visitors arrive.
usage.zh: 常在不速之客到来时用作警示。

text: 内行看门道，外行看热闹
pinyin: nèi háng kàn mén dào, wài háng kàn rè nao
literal: insider · look at · tricks, outsider · look at · excitement
natural: experts see the craft, laymen see the show

meaning.en: Experts notice the technique; amateurs only see the spectacle.
meaning.zh: 懂行的人看到其中的技巧和门道，不懂行的人只看表面的热闹。

equivalents: a layman sees the show, an expert sees the skill

examples.zh: 内行看门道，外行看热闹，他一眼就看出这幅画是真迹。
examples.en: Experts see the craft and laymen the show; he saw at once that painting was genuine.

examples.zh: 内行看门道，外行看热闹，我只觉得球赛精彩。
examples.en: I only thought the match was exciting; experts see the tactics.

usage.en: Explains the gap between experts and onlookers.
usage.zh: 说明行家与外行的差别。

synonyms: 行家一出手，便知有没有

pinyin: liǎng guó xiāng zhēng, bù zhǎn lái shǐ
literal: two · states · fight, not · kill · coming · envoy
natural: when states are at war, envoys are not killed

meaning.en: Even in conflict, messengers sent by the other side should not be harmed.
meaning.zh: 即使两国交战，也不杀对方派来的使者。

examples.zh: 两国相争，不斩来使，我们不能为难谈判代表。
examples.en: In war, envoys are spared; we can't make life hard for the negotiators.

examples.zh: 两国相争，不斩来使，这是历史上的惯例。
examples.en: Envoys are not killed even when states fight, according to old custom.

usage.en: Applied to any dispute where a go-between should be treated fairly.
usage.zh: 可用于任何需要善待传话人的场合。

pinyin: yuān yuān xiāng bào hé shí liǎo
literal: grievance · grievance · repay · when · end
natural: when will vengeance for vengeance end?

meaning.en: Revenge only breeds more revenge, so the cycle never ends.
meaning.zh: 冤仇互相报复，什么时候才是个头。

equivalents: an eye for an eye leaves the world blind

examples.zh: 冤冤相报何时了，不如放下恩怨。
examples.en: When will revenge ever end; better let the grudge go.

examples.zh: 电影结尾点明了冤冤相报何时了的主题。
examples.en: The film ends on the theme that vengeance has no end.

usage.en: Persuades people to give up grudges; often followed by 得饶人处且饶人.
usage.zh: 劝人放下仇怨，常接“得饶人处且饶人”。

pinyin: chū lái hùn, chí zǎo yào huán de
literal: come out · knock about, sooner or later · must · repay · (particle)
natural: if you knock about, you'll pay it back sooner or later

meaning.en: Those who live by wrongdoing will eventually pay for it.
meaning.zh: 做了坏事，早晚要付出代价。

examples.zh: 出来混，迟早要还的，他欠的债总有一天会来找他。
examples.en: What goes around comes around; his debts will catch up with him one day.

examples.zh: 别以为没人发现，出来混，迟早要还的。
examples.en: Don't think nobody noticed: you'll pay sooner or later.

usage.en: Popular from gangster films; casual, with a menacing edge.
usage.zh: 因黑帮电影流行，口语，带威胁意味。

pinyin: dà rén bù jì xiǎo rén guò
literal: great · person · not · remember · petty · person's · fault
natural: a big person doesn't remember a small person's faults

meaning.en: A magnanimous person does not hold a grudge over the mistakes of lesser people.
meaning.zh: 有气量的人不计较小人物的过错。

examples.zh: 大人不记小人过，请原谅我的无礼。
examples.en: A big person forgives a small one's faults; please excuse my rudeness.

examples.zh: 大人不记小人过，你就别跟他计较了。
examples.en: Be magnanimous; don't take it up with him.

usage.en: Used to ask for or offer forgiveness; often half-jokingly.
usage.zh: 用于求谅解或表示宽容，常半开玩笑。

pinyin: dī tóu bù jiàn tái tóu jiàn
literal: lower · head · not · see · raise · head · see
natural: you don't see them with head down, you do with head up

meaning.en: People who live or work close together will keep meeting, so keep relations civil.
meaning.zh: 天天碰面的人，免不了要打交道，所以要维持好关系。

examples.zh: 低头不见抬头见，邻里之间别闹僵。
examples.en: You'll meet every day; don't fall out with the neighbours.

examples.zh: 低头不见抬头见，同事何必计较。
examples.en: We see each other daily; why hold a grudge against colleagues?

usage.en: Used to advocate good terms with neighbours and colleagues.
usage.zh: 劝人与邻居、同事和睦相处。

pinyin: nǎ hú bù kāi tí nǎ hú
literal: which · kettle · not · boiling · lift · that · kettle
natural: lifting the kettle that isn't boiling

meaning.en: To mention exactly the thing that someone does not want to hear about.
meaning.zh: 偏偏提起别人最不愿提的事。

equivalents: to rub salt in the wound

examples.zh: 他刚失恋，你还问女朋友，哪壶不开提哪壶。
examples.en: He's just been dumped and you ask about his girlfriend; you touched his sore spot.

examples.zh: 别哪壶不开提哪壶，他最怕谈工资。
examples.en: Don't poke the sore spot; he hates talking about pay.

usage.en: A rebuke for tactlessness; often as 哪壶不开提哪壶 on its own.
usage.zh: 批评说话不顾忌，常单用。

text: 哑巴吃黄连，有苦说不出
pinyin: yǎ ba chī huáng lián, yǒu kǔ shuō bù chū
literal: mute · eat · coptis root, have · bitterness · say · not · out
natural: a mute eating bitter herbs can't voice the bitterness

meaning.en: To suffer a wrong or hardship that you cannot speak about.
meaning.zh: 受了委屈或有苦衷，却没法说出来。

examples.zh: 被冤枉了还不能解释，真是哑巴吃黄连，有苦说不出。
examples.en: Wrongly accused and unable to explain: suffering in silence.

examples.zh: 生意亏了，他哑巴吃黄连，有苦说不出。
examples.en: The business lost money and he suffers in silence.

usage.en: Originally a 歇后语 (哑巴吃黄连——有苦说不出); usually quoted in full.
usage.zh: 原为歇后语“哑巴吃黄连——有苦说不出”，现常整句使用。

pinyin: dà nàn bù sǐ, bì yǒu hòu fú
literal: great · disaster · not · die, surely · have · later · fortune
natural: survive a great disaster and good fortune will follow

meaning.en: Someone who survives a great calamity will be blessed afterwards.
meaning.zh: 经历大灾难而活下来的人，以后一定有福气。

equivalents: after the storm comes the calm

examples.zh: 你能平安出院，大难不死，必有后福。
examples.en: You came safely out of hospital; survive a great disaster and blessings follow.

examples.zh: 大难不死，必有后福，他后来事业越做越好。
examples.en: He survived the disaster and later his career went from strength to strength.

usage.en: Said to comfort or congratulate a survivor.
usage.zh: 安慰或祝贺劫后余生的人。

pinyin: nǚ zǐ wú cái biàn shì dé
literal: woman · lacking · talent · precisely · is · virtue
natural: a woman without talent is a virtuous woman

meaning.en: An outdated view that women should not be educated, as ignorance is a virtue.
meaning.zh: 旧时认为女子不读书、没有才学才是美德。

equivalents: a woman's place is in the home

examples.zh: 女子无才便是德是旧时代的偏见。
examples.en: 'A woman without talent is virtuous' is an old prejudice.

examples.zh: 现在没人再信女子无才便是德，女孩子都要读书。
examples.en: Nobody believes 'a woman is virtuous without talent' any more; girls must study.

usage.en: Today quoted only to criticise the old patriarchal view.
usage.zh: 现在多用来批判旧时男尊女卑的观念。

pinyin: hǎo hàn bù tí dāng nián yǒng
literal: true hero · not · mention · past · years' · valour
natural: a true hero doesn't brag of his past valour

meaning.en: A real man doesn't boast about former glory.
meaning.zh: 有本事的人不夸耀过去的功绩。

examples.zh: 好汉不提当年勇，你该看看现在的成绩。
examples.en: A real hero doesn't brag of past glory; look at your results now.

examples.zh: 爷爷从不说好汉不提当年勇的事。
examples.en: Grandpa never speaks of his glory days.

usage.en: Often teasing someone who boasts of past glory.
usage.zh: 常用来调侃总爱炫耀过去的人。

pinyin: yǒu jiè yǒu huán, zài jiè bù nán
literal: have · borrow · have · return, again · borrow · not · hard
natural: repay what you borrow and borrowing again is easy

meaning.en: If you return what you borrow, you can borrow again.
meaning.zh: 借了东西按时归还，下次再借就不难了。

equivalents: he that goes a-borrowing goes a-sorrowing

examples.zh: 有借有还，再借不难，我下周一定还你。
examples.en: Repay and you can borrow again; I'll certainly return it next week.

examples.zh: 有借有还，再借不难，信用最重要。
examples.en: Return what you borrow and you can borrow again; trust matters most.

usage.en: Used when promising to repay or urging others to.
usage.zh: 用于承诺归还或劝人守信。

pinyin: jiā huā méi yǒu yě huā xiāng
literal: home · flower · not · have · wild · flower · fragrance
natural: home flowers don't smell as sweet as wild ones

meaning.en: A cynical saying that the forbidden or novel seems more attractive than what one has.
meaning.zh: 旧指男子觉得别的女人比自己妻子有吸引力；泛指新鲜的、得不到的东西更诱人。

equivalents: the grass is always greener on the other side

examples.zh: 他总觉得家花没有野花香，最后婚姻破裂。
examples.en: He kept thinking home flowers smell less sweet, and the marriage broke down.

examples.zh: 别信家花没有野花香这种鬼话。
examples.en: Don't believe the rubbish that wild flowers smell sweeter.

usage.en: Typically used to criticise unfaithfulness; sexist in origin.
usage.zh: 多用于批评不忠，原带有大男子主义色彩。

pinyin: dǎ gǒu hái děi kàn zhǔ rén
literal: hit · dog · still · must · look at · owner
natural: before beating a dog, consider its owner

meaning.en: When you punish someone's subordinate, take their master's feelings into account.
meaning.zh: 惩罚别人的手下，也要顾及他主人的面子。

equivalents: don't hit the dog in front of its master

examples.zh: 打狗还得看主人，你不能这样对他的助理。
examples.en: Think of the owner before you hit the dog; you can't treat his assistant this way.

examples.zh: 打狗还得看主人，她背后有大领导撑腰。
examples.en: Mind the master before hitting the dog; she has a senior boss behind her.

usage.en: Often a warning about offending someone through their people.
usage.zh: 常告诫别得罪他人的亲信。

text: 授人以鱼不如授人以渔
pinyin: shòu rén yǐ yú bù rú shòu rén yǐ yú
variants: 授之以鱼不如授之以渔
literal: give · people · fish · not · as good as · teach · people · to fish
natural: teaching a man to fish beats giving him fish

meaning.en: Teaching someone a skill is better than simply handing them a result.
meaning.zh: 给人鱼吃，不如教他钓鱼；教方法比给结果更有用。

equivalents: give a man a fish and he eats for a day; teach him to fish and he eats for a lifetime

examples.zh: 授人以鱼不如授人以渔，老师教我们怎么学习。
examples.en: Teaching how to fish beats giving fish; the teacher shows us how to learn.

examples.zh: 扶贫要授人以鱼不如授人以渔，培训技能才有效。
examples.en: Teaching beats handing out; training skills is what works in poverty relief.

usage.en: A staple of teaching, parenting and aid discussion. Often tied to Laozi though the wording is later.
usage.zh: 常见于教育、扶贫等话题，常被附会为老子所说，措辞实为后起。

text: 又要马儿跑，又要马儿不吃草
pinyin: yòu yào mǎ ér pǎo, yòu yào mǎ ér bù chī cǎo
variants: 又要马儿好，又要马儿不吃草
literal: both · want · horse · run, both · want · horse · not · eat · grass
natural: wanting the horse to run yet not eat grass

meaning.en: To demand results without providing the necessary resources.
meaning.zh: 既要人出力，又不肯给好处；要求太高却不肯付出。

equivalents: you can't have your cake and eat it

examples.zh: 又要马儿跑，又要马儿不吃草，这怎么可能？
examples.en: Wanting the horse to run without feeding it is impossible.

examples.zh: 老板想要高质量又不加预算，又要马儿跑，又要马儿不吃草。
examples.en: The boss wants quality without extra budget: a horse that runs without grass.

usage.en: Complaint about unreasonable demands, often by workers.
usage.zh: 多为员工抱怨苛刻要求。

text: 吃人家的嘴软，拿人家的手短
pinyin: chī rén jiā de zuǐ ruǎn, ná rén jiā de shǒu duǎn
literal: eat · others' · mouth · soft, take · others' · hand · short
natural: who eats another's food speaks softly, who takes another's gifts is short-handed

meaning.en: If you accept favours or gifts, it is hard to refuse or criticise the giver.
meaning.zh: 收了别人的好处，就不好意思拒绝或批评他们。

equivalents: he who pays the piper calls the tune

examples.zh: 吃人家的嘴软，拿人家的手短，他不敢批评请客的人。
examples.en: Whoever eats another's food speaks softly; he dares not criticise the host.

examples.zh: 官员不能收礼，吃人家的嘴软，拿人家的手短。
examples.en: Officials mustn't take gifts: once you accept favours you're beholden.

usage.en: Common in anti-corruption talk.
usage.zh: 常见于廉政话题。

pinyin: hǎo jì xìng bù rú làn bǐ tóu
literal: good · memory · not · as good as · worn-out · pen
natural: a good memory is no match for a worn-out pen

meaning.en: Writing things down is more reliable than trusting memory.
meaning.zh: 再好的记忆力也比不上随手记下来可靠。

equivalents: the faintest ink is better than the best memory

examples.zh: 好记性不如烂笔头，开会要多做笔记。
examples.en: A good memory can't beat a worn pen; take notes in meetings.

examples.zh: 好记性不如烂笔头，我把地址写下来了。
examples.en: I wrote down the address, since a pen beats a good memory.

usage.en: Advice for students and workers.
usage.zh: 对学生和上班族的建议。

text: 常在河边走，哪有不湿鞋
pinyin: cháng zài hé biān zǒu, nǎ yǒu bù shī xié
literal: often · at · river · side · walk, how · have · not · wet · shoes
natural: if you often walk by the river, your shoes will get wet

meaning.en: If you are constantly exposed to temptation or risk, you'll eventually be caught up in it.
meaning.zh: 长期处在有风险或诱惑的环境里，难免出问题。

equivalents: he who plays with fire gets burned
if you hang around the barber's, you'll get a haircut

examples.zh: 常在河边走，哪有不湿鞋，他在这行干久了，最终还是出了事。
examples.en: Walk by the river long enough and your shoes get wet; he eventually got into trouble.

examples.zh: 常在河边走，哪有不湿鞋，你少和他们混。
examples.en: Keep on walking along the river and you'll get wet; stay away from them.

usage.en: Often cautions about risky circles; usually said with a hint of sarcasm.
usage.zh: 多提醒人远离风险圈子，常带讽刺。

pinyin: tiáo tiáo dà lù tōng luó mǎ
literal: every · big · road · lead to · Rome
natural: all roads lead to Rome

meaning.en: There are many ways to reach the same goal.
meaning.zh: 达到目标的途径有很多条。

equivalents: there's more than one way to skin a cat

examples.zh: 条条大路通罗马，你不一定要走他的路。
examples.en: All roads lead to Rome; you don't have to follow his way.

examples.zh: 条条大路通罗马，这次没考上还有别的路。
examples.en: All roads lead to Rome; if you failed this time there are other ways.

usage.en: Translated from the Western proverb.
usage.zh: 译自西方谚语。

pinyin: sǐ yào miàn zi huó shòu zuì
literal: to the death · want · face · alive · suffer
natural: clinging to face and suffering in life

meaning.en: To suffer needlessly because you insist on saving face.
meaning.zh: 为了面子硬撑，结果自己吃苦。

equivalents: cut off your nose to spite your face

examples.zh: 明明没钱还请客，真是死要面子活受罪。
examples.en: He's broke yet treats everyone: suffering for the sake of face.

examples.zh: 死要面子活受罪，何必硬撑着不肯求助。
examples.en: Why suffer to save face and refuse help?

usage.en: Critical or teasing; casual.
usage.zh: 批评或调侃，口语。

pinyin: sǐ zhū bù pà kāi shuǐ tàng
literal: dead · pig · not · fear · boiling · water · scald
natural: a dead pig doesn't fear scalding water

meaning.en: Someone beyond caring or shame can't be threatened by punishment.
meaning.zh: 已经破罐破摔的人，什么惩罚、批评也不怕了。

examples.zh: 他欠了一屁股债，死猪不怕开水烫，催债也没用。
examples.en: He's deep in debt; a dead pig fears no boiling water, so chasing him is useless.

examples.zh: 死猪不怕开水烫，罚他也无所谓。
examples.en: He's past caring about punishment.

usage.en: Describes a defiantly shameless attitude; casual and derogatory.
usage.zh: 形容满不在乎、无所畏惧的无赖态度，口语，贬义。
